correctness.rationale: The selected-degree≤1 condition exactly characterizes the faces. The projection onto hub and original rim vertices is monotone, and every matched incidence toggles one subdivision vertex and is an actual face-poset cover. In a hub fiber at most one original rim vertex is selected; at least n−2 subdivision vertices can be toggled freely. Without the hub, a subdivision vertex joining two selected rim vertices is forbidden. The only pair exclusions left come from the two subdivision neighbors of an isolated selected rim vertex, so the pairs are disjoint. If any allowed subdivision vertex lies in no pair, its toggle matches the whole fiber. Otherwise all rim vertices are selected, or the proper cyclic word has no 00 (which leaves an isolated allowed vertex) and no 11 (a boundary of that run leaves one). This forces exactly the two alternating words for even n, and none for odd n. In each alternating fiber choose one endpoint of each forbidden pair in an ordered list and apply sequential element matching. Equivalently, toggle the chosen endpoint of the first pair whose other endpoint is absent. Only the face containing every other endpoint survives, of size n. The all-selected rim fiber also contributes one size-n face. Patchwork gives acyclicity; restriction to the ordinary nonempty face poset makes the singleton formerly paired with the empty face critical and retains the other pairs. Thus the Morse CW complex has one vertex and one or three (n−1)-cells, attached to a point, proving the sphere wedge without any coefficient assumption. The frozen self-review uses ‘critical facets’ loosely: for n=4 a legitimate alternating unmatched face {u₀,u₂,w₂,w₃} can be extended by u₁. The primary proof correctly says critical faces and needs no facet claim.

reproduction.result: Checked all faces, pair involutions, exceptional fibers and every directed Hasse incidence for 3≤n≤9; reduced Euler characteristics in order are +1,−3,+1,−3,+1,−3,+1. For 3≤n≤7 independent signed rational and mod-two boundary ranks give β₀=1 and the predicted β_(n−1), with no other Betti numbers. This is not integral Smith reduction or an all-n proof; the CW argument supplies integral homotopy. The frozen verifier was inspected, not run.

evidence: Sawant treats vertex decomposability on trees. Deshpande–Singh treat complete multipartite, fully whiskered, path, cycle and perfect-tree families; their cycle theorem takes the ordinary cycle as input.
The literature search returned subdivision/Alexander-dual results for ordinary independence complexes, not the Ind₂ statement needed here.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The induced 2n-cycle in the gear rim excludes trees, while the hub and degree-three rim vertices distinguish the gear from a cycle. There are no leaves, and this bipartite graph is not complete bipartite. Neither those graph scopes nor ordinary independence results imply this Ind₂ wedge count.

value.rationale: This is the homotopy type of a natural cyclic hub-and-rim family at its first higher-independence threshold, in unbounded dimension. A complete family classification with parity changing the number of spheres from one to three is stronger than Euler data or field homology; the proof identifies the exact cyclic-word obstruction using a short uniform matching. It neither promises higher-threshold results nor depends on such promises for value.
